predecessors.name: Transpadane Republic
predecessors.text: the state north of the Po that Napoleon set up after Lodi (May 1796), enlarged on 19 May 1797 with the territories of the former Duchy of Modena

predecessors.name: Cispadane Republic
predecessors.text: 'The rest of Cispadania was merged into the Cisalpine Republic on 27 July' 1797

successors.name: Italian Republic (Kingdom of Italy from 1805)
successors.text: the whole republic, renamed on 26 January 1802

ledger.x: 1797: the Romagna passes from the Pope.
29 June 1797: Napoleon decrees the Cisalpine Republic at Milan.
19 May 1797 (before the decree): Modena passes to Transpadania.
27 July 1797: the Cispadane Republic joins the Cisalpine.
22 October 1797: the Valtellina joins the Republic.
26 May 1798: the Mincio department (Mantua) is added.
27 April 1799: the Austro-Russian army takes the republic after Cassano.
26 January 1802: the Cisalpine Republic becomes the Italian Republic.

wars.name: Italian campaign of 1796-1797 (War of the First Coalition)
wars.outcome: Beaulieu's Austrians lost Lodi on 10 May 1796; Sardinia accepted the Armistice of Cherasco on 28 April; Austria asked for the Peace of Leoben (18 April 1797) and signed Campo Formio on 17 October 1797, acknowledging the Cisalpine Republic.

wars.name: Austro-Russian conquest of northern Italy
wars.outcome: After Cassano the Cisalpine Republic was occupied by Suvorov's forces; Napoleon restored it in June 1800 and the Treaty of Luneville (9 February 1801) set the frontier with the Holy Roman Empire 'on the River Adige'.

certainty.note: Departmental lists with dates (eleven departments in 1797, Mincio 1798, Novara 1800) and the Adige frontier of 9 February 1801.
